topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: op-sync-tester — reimplement the OP-aware PayloadID hash (drop op-geth miner)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Context

`op-sync-tester` is a CL-facing EL **mock** (it proxies a real EL — op-reth in sysgo tests — and gates block visibility by session heads to test op-node/supernode sync). It performs **no block building or execution**, yet it imports op-geth's heavy `miner` package for exactly one thing: `miner.BuildPayloadArgs{…}.Id()`, to compute the `PayloadID` it returns from `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` so the value matches what the real EL would produce ([`op-sync-tester/synctester/backend/sync_tester.go#L485-L507`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/61cc3034923bba60d68c66f25dab0c2d5b0737aa/op-sync-tester/synctester/backend/sync_tester.go#L485-L507)).

This is the only op-geth dependency in op-sync-tester that is **not** a plain call-site swap, so it gets its own tracking issue. (The eip1559 call-site swap is already done in #21500. The remaining `core/types` / `beacon/engine` / `params.ChainConfig` swaps ride with the general call-site work in #20263 and the `op-service/eth.BlockAsPayload` decoupling — they share the `ChainConfig` signature.)

## Why a reimplementation is needed (not just upstream's `miner`)

op-geth's `BuildPayloadArgs.Id()` hashes **five OP-Stack-specific fields** that upstream go-ethereum's `Id()` does not: `NoTxPool`, `Transactions`, `GasLimit`, `EIP1559Params` (Holocene), and `MinBaseFee` (Jovian). After the final go.mod cutover to upstream go-ethereum (#20266), upstream's `Id()` would omit these and compute a `PayloadID` that **does not match op-reth** (which is OP-aware), so the mock CL could not resolve the ID returned from FCU-with-attributes. We must therefore carry an OP-aware `Id()` reimplementation rather than fall back to upstream's `miner`.

## Scope

- Reimplement the OP-aware `PayloadID` hash (the standard fields + the five OP additions) — either a small helper in `op-core` (e.g. alongside the engine/payload types) or local to op-sync-tester — and use it in `sync_tester.go`, removing the `github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/miner` import entirely.
- Add a differential test asserting byte-identical IDs vs op-geth's `miner.BuildPayloadArgs.Id()` over a range of args (Canyon/Holocene/Jovian permutations). Remove it at the cutover, like the other op-core differential tests.
- **Verify/fix a latent gap while here:** the current construction sets `EIP1559Params` (Holocene) but never sets `MinBaseFee`, so a Jovian block carrying a min base fee would already get a `PayloadID` that disagrees with the real EL. The reimplementation should wire `MinBaseFee` from the attributes/block.

## Effort

Small (~0.5 day). No execution semantics to reproduce — the hash is pure `sha256`/RLP over the args.

Part of #20257.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topIssues.title: kona-gossip: Apply peer, address and subnet blocks to inbound and existing connections
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
kona-node's peer, address and subnet blocks (`opp2p_blockPeer`, `opp2p_blockAddr`, `opp2p_blockSubnet`) only stop the node from dialing out. A blocked peer can still connect to us, and blocking a peer we're already connected to leaves the connection open. Found while working on #23430.

### Current behaviour
- **Only our own dials are checked.** `ConnectionGater::can_dial` ([gater.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/gater.rs#L270)) checks the blocklists, but only `GossipDriver::dial_multiaddr` calls it. The swarm's `Behaviour` (ping, gossipsub, identify, the sync stream; [behaviour.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/behaviour.rs#L33)) has nothing that looks at incoming connections. The driver doesn't handle `SwarmEvent::IncomingConnection`, and `ConnectionEstablished` doesn't check the blocklists either ([driver.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/driver.rs#L494)).
- **Blocked addresses and subnets do nothing for incoming connections.** `BlockAddr` and `BlockSubnet` only update the gater ([command.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/rpc/command.rs#L82-L85)).
- **Blocked peers are only muted.** `BlockPeer` also adds the peer to gossipsub's blacklist ([command.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/rpc/command.rs#L74)), so its gossip is ignored. But the connection is accepted, stays open, and still carries identify, ping and the sync request/response protocol.
- **Blocking doesn't disconnect.** None of the three commands closes an existing connection. The operator has to call `opp2p_disconnectPeer` as well, and for an address or subnet first find out which peers are connected from it.

### What op-node does
go-libp2p's connection gater, which op-node wraps for expiry and metrics (`op-node/p2p/gating`), checks both directions: `InterceptAccept` refuses an incoming connection from a blocked IP or subnet before the handshake, and `InterceptSecured` refuses it once the handshake reveals a blocked peer ID (`p2p/net/conngater/conngater.go`).

### Proposal
- **Check incoming connections.** Add a small `NetworkBehaviour` to `Behaviour` that asks the gater: `handle_pending_inbound_connection` refuses a remote address with a blocked IP or subnet, and `handle_established_inbound_connection` refuses a blocked peer ID. `libp2p::allow_block_list` only covers peer IDs, so it isn't enough by itself.
- **Disconnect on block.** `BlockPeer` closes the peer's connections. `BlockAddr` and `BlockSubnet` close the connections whose remote address is in the blocked range.
- **Static peers (#23430)** follow the block too: a blocked static peer isn't dialed, or let back in, until it's unblocked.

### Tests
- An incoming connection from a blocked peer, address or subnet is refused.
- Blocking a connected peer, or the address or subnet it's connected from, closes the connection.
- After unblocking, the peer can connect again.

Related: #23700, which adds connection limits that would live in the same place.

topIssues.title: kona-gossip: Remove the write-only connectedness map from ConnectionGater
topIssues.author: aakoshh
topIssues.body:
`ConnectionGater` keeps a `connectedness: HashMap<PeerId, Connectedness>` that nothing reads. Found while working on #23430.

### Current behaviour
- **Written** by `dialing` (as `Connected`, before the dial has succeeded), by refusals for a blocked IP or subnet or the redial limit (`CannotConnect`), and by `block_peer`/`unblock_peer` ([gater.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/gater.rs#L251)).
- **Never read:** `ConnectionGate::connectedness()` ([gater.rs](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/0130abb2f07230ce01c904ba2fbb5d6338ba549f/rust/kona/crates/node/gossip/src/gater.rs#L315)) has no callers. The `opp2p_peers` RPC works connectedness out from the swarm's connected peers and the gater's blocked peers instead.
- **Never shrinks:** entries are never removed, so the map grows with every peer the node ever dials. #23700 covers that side.

### Why the map isn't needed
The `Connectedness` enum mirrors go-libp2p's (`NotConnected`, `Connected`, `CanConnect`, `CannotConnect`, `Limited`, with the same numbers), so `opp2p_peers` responses match op-node's. That's worth keeping. But go-libp2p has deprecated `CanConnect` and `CannotConnect`, and its swarm works connectedness out from open connections on every call: it only ever returns `Connected`, `Limited` or `NotConnected`. op-node keeps no connection history, so this map has nothing to match.

### Proposal
- Remove the `connectedness` map and `ConnectionGate::connectedness()`. That's a breaking change to the `ConnectionGate` trait.
- Optionally, report blocked peers as `NotConnected` in `opp2p_peers`, as op-node does. kona reports `CannotConnect` today.

topIssues.title: contracts-bedrock: remove ETHLockbox gating once every chain uses the lockbox
topIssues.author: lumoswiz
topIssues.body:
`OPContractsManagerV2.upgrade()` [enables the ETHLockbox on every chain it upgrades](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/fc07be300dd8792d0226b3804b770b9cb66c1b0b/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/opcm/OPContractsManagerV2.sol#L905-L953). Once every chain uses the lockbox, `OptimismPortal2._isUsingLockbox()` should always return true.

- Confirm that `_isFeatureEnabled(Features.ETH_LOCKBOX)` and `address(ethLockbox) != address(0)` are always true on every chain after the upgrade.
- Once confirmed, remove the redundant checks and no-lockbox branches, keeping the lockbox behavior unconditional. Remove tests for the no-lockbox paths.

Follow-up to [review feedback on #23736](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23736#discussion_r4427501348).

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: run TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset against kona-node
topIssues.author: joshklop
topIssues.body:
## Summary

[`TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/op-acceptance-tests/tests/sync/elsync/offset_el_safe/sync_test.go) is skipped when the acceptance suite runs against kona-node (`sysgo.SkipOnKonaNode(t, "kona-node does not support OffsetELSafe")`, added in https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23827).

The test configures the verifier with `OffsetELSafe`, which maps to op-node's `--syncmode.offset-el-safe`. After EL sync completes, op-node holds the safe and finalized heads that far behind the synced tip. The flag defaults to 12h, matching the OP Mainnet sequencing window. kona-node has no equivalent option, and devstack rejects the setting for kona-node with `unsupported L2CL option for kona-node` (`op-devstack/sysgo/l2_cl_kona_config.go`).

Until https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23827, the test was skipped on op-reth, and op-geth skips every chain that activates Karst. So this gap was never reached in any CI configuration.

## Required work

Implement the EL-sync safe/finalized offset in kona-node with the same semantics and default as op-node. Wire it through the devstack kona-node config, then remove the kona-node skip.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] kona-node supports an EL-sync safe/finalized offset matching op-node's `--syncmode.offset-el-safe` semantics and default.
- [ ] `op-devstack/sysgo/l2_cl_kona_config.go` accepts `OffsetELSafe` for kona-node.
- [ ] The kona-node skip is removed and `TestELSyncSafeRetractedByOffset` passes against kona-node.
- [ ] Existing op-node coverage continues to pass.

## Related

- https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/23827
- Parent inventory: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/101

topPRs.title: kona-gossip,kona-rpc!: Enforce peer, address and subnet blocks on inbound and existing connections
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
### What

kona-node now enforces the operator's peer, address and subnet blocks, and score bans, on inbound connections and on connections that are already open, not only on its own dials. `opp2p_connectPeer` and `opp2p_disconnectPeer` now wait for the result and report why a connection fails.

### Why

Before this PR, a block only stopped kona's own dials. A blocked peer, or a peer at a blocked address, could still dial in, and an open connection stayed open after its peer was blocked. A score ban disconnected the peer, but nothing kept it from reconnecting at once.

For operators:
- **Blocks** (`opp2p_blockPeer`, `opp2p_blockAddr`, `opp2p_blockSubnet`) refuse inbound connections, by address before the handshake, and close existing connections in both directions. They also apply to protected and static peers. op-node, by contrast, leaves open connections in place. A block that covers a static peer is logged as a warning.
- **Score bans** (`--p2p.ban.peers`) refuse the peer in both directions until the ban expires. As in op-node, `opp2p_unblockPeer` lifts a ban, and bans aren't listed by `opp2p_listBlockedPeers`.
- **`opp2p_connectPeer`** used to fail at once with "Peer not connected" for any peer, because its poll never retried. It now waits up to 30 seconds for the connection, as op-node does, fails at once with the gate's reason for a blocked or banned peer, and returns the dial's error when the dial fails. **`opp2p_disconnectPeer`** waits for the connections to close. Both return only once the P2P RPC's state shows the change, so an `opp2p_peers` call right after lists it. The devstack's `connectL2CLPeers` relies on that.
- **RPC errors:** these two methods' failures now use code `-32000` with the reason, as op-node's do, where they used `-32602` (invalid params) with "Peer not connected" or "Peers are still connected". An address that names no peer, or has nothing to dial before its `/p2p/<peer id>`, is still `-32602`, with a message saying which.
- **`opp2p_peers`** reports `latency` in nanoseconds, as op-node does. It was in whole seconds, so always `0`.
- **The `payload_by_number` sync protocol is no longer served.** op-node retired both its client and its server. kona's stub read each request without a size limit or timeout, so a peer could stream bytes into the node until it ran out of memory.
- **Metrics:** `kona_node_gossip_inbound_connections_refused` is new, by `reason`. `kona_node_dial_peer_error{type="already_connected"}` now counts less, since `opp2p_connectPeer` to a connected peer no longer dials.
- **Logs:** peers connecting and disconnecting are logged at debug, no longer at info and warn. A gossip listener that closes while the node runs is logged as an error.
- **The P2P RPC** answers from gossip state up to a second old. What a command changes shows at once, and so do connection, identify, subscription and address changes. If the network actor doesn't publish fresher state within two seconds, a call answers from the last state.

Closes #23715. Closes #23701.

### How

- **The blocks live in `gate::Behaviour`, a `NetworkBehaviour`,** the first field of the gossip `Behaviour`. The swarm asks its behaviours about a connection in `handle_pending_inbound_connection`, before the handshake, and in `handle_established_*_connection`, once the peer ID is known. These are the only points where a connection can be refused. By the time the driver sees `ConnectionEstablished`, gossipsub has already queued its subscriptions, so the driver could only close the connection again. Being the first field means the gate is asked before gossipsub, identify and ping.
- **`ConnectionGater` keeps only the dial bookkeeping,** and checks the gate it is given. The gater's write-only `connectedness` map is gone (#23701).
- **The RPC's gossip snapshot is built on demand.** The network actor used to rebuild it after every step: for each gossip message, ping and identify event. It now publishes after each command, and when a reader asks for one fresher than the reader's `max_age`, through a refresh channel with room for one request, so readers that ask at the same time share one build. It also publishes when the swarm reports a change the snapshot shows.
- **`ConnectPeer` and `DisconnectPeer` carry a reply,** which the driver answers from the swarm event that settles the outcome. `ConnectPeer` carries a `PeerAddr`, so the RPC parses the address once. A refusal by the gate, before the dial or once the connection is established, comes back typed, as `ConnectPeerError::Refused`.
- **`GossipDriver::start` returns a `PeerAddr`,** which always ends in the node's peer ID.
- **The devstack's `TestP2PPeers`** expected a blocked peer to stay connected, as in op-node. On kona nodes, it now waits for the connection to close, and reconnects the peer after unblocking it.

### Caveats

- A peer refused by its peer ID still completes the Noise handshake, since the ID is only known after it. op-node's `InterceptSecured` works the same way. Address and subnet blocks refuse before the handshake.
- A static peer given by a DNS name can't be matched against an address block until it is connected, so the warning about blocking it may not appear.
- Blocks and bans don't survive a restart (#23768).
- Scores and ping latencies in RPC answers can be up to a second old, since they change without an event.
- A gossip listener that closes while the node runs is logged, but the node keeps running without it (#23793).
- op-node versions that still run the sync request client get "protocol not supported" from kona now, and may score it down. That client has been off by default since #18088, and was removed in op-node v1.19.1.
- The `opp2p_*` methods are served to anyone who can reach the RPC port, which listens on `0.0.0.0` by default, as in op-node. Blocks are stronger now, so `opp2p_blockSubnet 0.0.0.0/0` cuts the node off from every peer (#23798).
- The gossip peerstore keeps every peer that ever completed identify. This PR also stops removing a banned peer's entry, for parity with op-node (#23800).

### Alternatives

- **The blocklist as shared state in the driver** (`Arc<RwLock>`): rejected, because the driver only sees a connection after it is established, and can't refuse it before.
- **Bounding the sync stub instead of removing it:** done first, in its own commit (read exactly the 8-byte request, with op-node's 10-second deadline), then removed, since op-node no longer uses the protocol.
- **Dialing an unblocked static peer at once:** rejected. `opp2p_connectPeer` covers the urgent case, and the driver would have needed another way to schedule its checks. The peer is dialed at the next check, within a minute.
- **Listing score bans in `opp2p_listBlockedPeers`:** rejected, for parity with op-node, and because a tool that copies blocks between nodes would turn temporary bans into permanent blocks. Making bans visible is #23796.

- **Dropping `test_sync_request_protocol_is_unsupported` once the protocol was gone,** as a review suggested: kept, so that a peer asking for the protocol is shown to get "protocol not supported", rather than a stream kona never answers.

### Potential follow-ups

- Split `kona-gossip/src/driver.rs`, now about 2,000 lines, into a module by concern, as a pure move.
- Move the JSON-RPC wire types (`PeerInfo`, `PeerDump`, ...) from `kona-gossip` to `kona-rpc`, or to an RPC-types crate.
- Make `GossipDriver` generic over its message handler. Today it knows OP payload types, the v1–v4 block topics and the signer rotation, and takes the chain ID from the block handler's rollup config.
- `NetworkActor::step` is hard to read and to test as one `select!`. The `next`/`handle` split proposed in #23534 and #23580 would help, for example for #23793.
- Filed: #23793 (stop the node when the gossip listener closes), #23796 (show score bans over the RPC, and the misleading `banned*` field names), #23797 (late blocks from the previous signer are rejected at a signer rotation), #23798 (don't serve the P2P control methods to anyone who can reach the RPC port), #23800 (prune disconnected peers from the peerstore), #23768 (keep blocks and bans across restarts, now with a startup warning about blocked static peers).

BREAKING CHANGE: Rust users of `kona-gossip` and `kona-rpc` need to update their code; the node's command-line flags and RPC methods don't change.
- The sync request/response protocol is gone, with `Behaviour::sync_req_resp`, `GossipDriverBuilderError::{SetupSyncReqRespError, SyncReqRespAlreadyAccepted}` and `Event::Stream`.
- `GossipDriver`'s `swarm`, `addr`, `handler` and `peerstore` fields are private, and `behaviour_mut` is gone. Use `addr()`, `handler()`, `peer_addr()`, `connected_peers()` (now the peer IDs, not a count), and the driver's `block_*`, `unblock_*` and `list_blocked_*` methods.
- `ConnectionGater`'s blocklist and `connectedness` fields, and the `ConnectionGate` trait's block, list and `connectedness` methods, are gone; `ConnectionGate::can_dial` takes the `gate::Behaviour`.
- `GossipDriver::start` returns a `PeerAddr`; `dial_peer` and `dial_multiaddr` return a `Result`.
- `GossipCommand::ConnectPeer` carries a `PeerAddr` named `peer` and a reply sender, and `DisconnectPeer` a reply sender. `GossipDriver::connect_peer` takes a `PeerAddr`.
- `NetworkActorError::DriverStartup` is gone; nothing returned it.
- `GossipQueryHandle::new` takes the refresh sender, and `GossipQueryHandle::snapshot` is async and takes the oldest snapshot age the caller accepts. `GossipState::pings` is a field.

topPRs.title: kona-node!: share one verified L1 client across the node
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
kona-node read L1 through several separately built clients, and with an untrusted L1 RPC it checked only block hashes. A dishonest or buggy L1 RPC could drop batcher transactions or deposits from what derivation sees, or install an unsafe block signer of its choosing, without any error. The node now reads L1 through one shared client with shared caches and a deadline on every request. Unless `--l1-trust-rpc` is set, it verifies what it reads against the block header, as op-node does: header hashes, block numbers, transactions and receipts roots, and an `eth_getProof` proof of the unsafe block signer.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/568

**Effect on operators**
- With `--l1-trust-rpc=false`, the default, the L1 RPC must serve `eth_getProof`, or the node fails to start. The README, the flag help and the operator docs now say so.
- L1 RPC metrics come from the transport.
  - `kona_providers_chain_rpc_calls` and `kona_providers_chain_rpc_errors` are replaced by `kona_rpc_client_request_duration_seconds{client, method, outcome, error}`.
  - `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes`, which nothing set, is removed.
  - The chain provider's cache metrics now use the `cache` label values `headers`, `receipts` and `transactions`.
  - The bundled dashboards are updated.
- After an L1 reorg, an engine reset no longer keeps an unsafe head whose L1 origin was reorged out. It checks the origin against the canonical block at that height, as op-node's `FindL2Heads` does.

**Fault-proof program.** `5c0560f886` changes `kona-derive`: a pipeline reset resolves its base by hash, as op-program does. That changes the preimages kona-client requests, so it changes the prestate. The `kona-sp1-cost-reviewer` found no limit risk: the witness is unchanged, and each reset adds a small constant cost.

**For reviewers.** Each commit is self-contained and builds and passes on its own. Each `!` commit's message states what breaks and how to migrate. Read in this order:
- the shared client, from `37d32512a6` to `64105bdc5f`;
- caching and metrics, `cc3c3cb0c3` and `7a19d1554a`;
- verification, from `fb1f04068d` to `4c8ce50961`, then `ea277a40a4`;
- the review fixes, from `09286ae49d`.

**Reviews.** I ran `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer`, `kona-sp1-cost-reviewer`, `safedb-reviewer` and a security review of the L1 verification against op-node. I skipped `deposit-reviewer` and `derivation-batch-reviewer`, because nothing here changes how deposits or batches are decoded. Findings dismissed, with the author's agreement:
- **The dashboard panel for `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes` is kept.** It was already empty before this PR.
- **The request deadline comes from the transport kona-node builds, not from `AlloyChainProvider` itself.** The requirement is documented on `L1ConfigBuilder::provider` and `AlloyChainProvider::new`. Moving the deadline into the provider crate can follow separately.
- **Two cleanups are left for later:** a shared `BlockInfo`-from-header constructor, and one helper for mapping a missing block to `None`.
- **`kona-engine` now depends on `kona-providers-alloy`.** This is intended: the engine reads L1 through the shared client.
- **The pipeline reset does not check its base block's number.** op-node does not either. When verifying, the hash already fixes the number, and any error kind there could loop in the fault-proof program.

Older gaps the reviews found are tracked in protocol-team: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/570, https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/571 and https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/572. The L2 provider's verification is https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/569.

BREAKING CHANGE: This affects operators, dashboards and code that uses kona's Rust crates.
- **Operators:** without `--l1-trust-rpc`, the L1 RPC must serve `eth_getProof`.
- **Dashboards and alerts:** they must move to the metrics above.
- **Rust API:**
  - `kona-providers-alloy`: `AlloyChainProvider`'s constructors and methods, new `AlloyChainProviderError` variants, the `Metrics` constants including `PROVIDER_REQUEST_DURATION`, and the free `unsafe_block_signer` function.
  - `kona-derive`: `ChainProvider::block_info_by_number_for_reset` is removed.
  - `kona-node-service`: the `DerivationDelegate*` exports, `L1Config`, `L1ConfigBuilder`, `BlockStream`, `L1WatcherActor` and `EngineConfig`.
  - `kona-engine`: the L1 methods on `EngineClient` and `EngineClientBuilder`.

Each `!` commit's message gives the exact change and the migration.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: kona-node!: share one L1 client across the node
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
kona-node read L1 through several separately built clients. Derivation, the sequencer, the L1 watcher, the engine and the unsafe block signer lookup each had their own connection, caches and timeouts, so the same L1 data was fetched and cached more than once, and some reads had no deadline. The node now builds one `AlloyChainProvider` at startup and shares it, so every L1 read goes through the same caches and one per-request deadline on the transport. This also gives L1 verification, in the next PR, a single place to live. The engine's sync-start check now reads the canonical L1 block by number through the shared client.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23745
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/579
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/580
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/581

**Stack.** This is part 3 of 5, split out of #23829. Merge them in order:
1. #23846: delete `DerivationDelegateClient`
2. #23847: check sync-start L1 origins against the canonical chain
3. #23848: share one L1 client across the node ← this PR
4. #23849: verify L1 RPC data against block headers
5. #23850: resolve pipeline reset bases by hash

**Effect on operators.** Nothing changes in what the node checks or what the L1 RPC must serve. The L1 metrics change:
- L1 RPC metrics come from the transport. `kona_providers_chain_rpc_calls` and `kona_providers_chain_rpc_errors` are replaced by `kona_rpc_client_request_duration_seconds{client, method, outcome, error}`. Its `method` label holds JSON-RPC method names, and failures that are not RPC errors, such as receipts that fail to decode, are no longer counted as errors.
- `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes`, which nothing set, is removed.
- The chain provider's cache metrics use new `cache` label values.
- The bundled dashboards are updated.

**For reviewers.** Each commit is self-contained and builds and passes on its own. Each `!` commit's message states what breaks and how to migrate. Read in this order:
- the shared client, from `e48420165c` to `71436310ff`;
- follow-ups to the provider's API, from `968103fdf4` to `ed8eefe1a2` (`213f446544` only ignores local Zed settings);
- caching and metrics, from `d51bac140e` to `9d86fb8c65`.

**Reviews.** These are #23829's commits, rebased past the moved reset change, plus a test helper that keeps kona-rpc's tests compiling at each commit. On #23829, `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer` and `safedb-reviewer` ran over them. Findings dismissed, with the author's agreement:
- **The dashboard panel for `kona_providers_cache_memory_bytes` is kept.** It was already empty before this PR.
- **The request deadline comes from the transport kona-node builds, not from `AlloyChainProvider` itself.** The requirement is documented on `L1ConfigBuilder::provider` and `AlloyChainProvider::new`. Moving the deadline into the provider crate can follow separately.
- **`kona-engine` now depends on `kona-providers-alloy`.** This is intended: the engine reads L1 through the shared client.

BREAKING CHANGE: This affects dashboards, alerts and code that uses kona's Rust crates.
- **Dashboards and alerts:** they must move to the metrics above.
- **Rust API:**
  - `kona-providers-alloy`: `AlloyChainProvider`'s constructors (`new_http` and the two-argument `new` are removed, and `cache_size` is a `NonZeroUsize`), its `inner` and `trust_rpc` are no longer public, the free `unsafe_block_signer` function is removed, and the `Metrics` constants for RPC calls, errors and cache memory are removed or renamed.
  - `kona-node-service`: `L1Config`, `L1ConfigBuilder`, `BlockStream`, `L1WatcherActor`, `DelayedL1OriginSelectorProvider`, `L1OriginSelectorError`, `EngineConfig` and `build_engine_client`.
  - `kona-engine`: the L1 methods on `EngineClient` and `EngineClientBuilder`, and a new `SyncStartError::L1` variant.

Each `!` commit's message gives the exact change and the migration.

topPRs.title: kona-node!: verify L1 RPC data against block headers
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
With an untrusted L1 RPC, kona-node checked only block hashes. A dishonest or buggy L1 RPC could drop batcher transactions or deposits from what derivation sees, or install an unsafe block signer of its choosing, without any error. Unless `--l1-trust-rpc` is set, the node now verifies what it reads through its shared L1 client against the block header, as op-node does: header hashes, block numbers, transactions and receipts roots, and an `eth_getProof` proof of the unsafe block signer.

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/568
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/582
Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/583

**Stack.** This is part 4 of 5, split out of #23829. Merge them in order:
1. #23846: delete `DerivationDelegateClient`
2. #23847: check sync-start L1 origins against the canonical chain
3. #23848: share one L1 client across the node
4. #23849: verify L1 RPC data against block headers ← this PR
5. #23850: resolve pipeline reset bases by hash

**Effect on operators**
- With `--l1-trust-rpc=false`, the default, the L1 RPC must serve `eth_getProof`, or the node fails to start. The README, the flag help and the operator docs now say so.
- The chain provider's cache metrics replace the `block_info_and_transactions` value of the `cache` label with `transactions`. The bundled dashboards are unaffected.
- The L1 watcher waits a full poll interval after each poll, so a slow L1 RPC is not polled again as soon as it answers.

Until the reset-by-hash PR above this one removes it, the pipeline reset's separate lookup by number goes through the same verification as every other lookup.

**For reviewers.** Each commit is self-contained and builds and passes on its own. Each `!` commit's message states what breaks and how to migrate. Read in this order:
- verification, from `1b33bce8ea` to `eca5df16df`, then `ae0ab3940b`;
- the review fixes, from `6ac3383d08`;
- the docs, `f6ed432cdc` and `d7b86a68ed`.

**Reviews.** On #23829, I ran `rust-code-reviewer`, `deletion-reviewer` and a security review of the L1 verification against op-node over these commits. Here they are unchanged, except that the reset lookup is routed through verification; `rust-code-reviewer` checked that change. I skipped `deposit-reviewer` and `derivation-batch-reviewer`, because nothing here changes how deposits or batches are decoded. Finding dismissed, with the author's agreement:
- **Two cleanups are left for later:** a shared `BlockInfo`-from-header constructor, and one helper for mapping a missing block to `None`.

Older gaps the reviews found are tracked in protocol-team: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/570, https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/571 and https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/572. The L2 provider's verification is https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/protocol-team/issues/569.

BREAKING CHANGE: This affects operators, dashboards and code that uses the `kona-providers-alloy` crate.
- **Operators:** without `--l1-trust-rpc`, the L1 RPC must serve `eth_getProof`.
- **Dashboards and alerts:** queries on the chain provider's cache metrics that filter on `cache="block_info_and_transactions"` must use `cache="transactions"`.
- **Rust API:** `AlloyChainProviderError` gains `HeaderHashMismatch`, `BlockNumberMismatch`, `TransactionsRootMismatch`, `ReceiptsRootMismatch` and `InvalidStorageProof`, and `EmptyRawReceiptsForNonEmptyBlock` loses its `transaction_count` field. `AlloyChainProvider::unsafe_block_signer` returns `Result<Address, AlloyChainProviderError>`. `AlloyChainProvider::latest_block_number` and `AlloyChainProvider::chain_id` are removed.

Each `!` commit's message gives the exact change and the migration.
